name: Sagrantino

lines.s10: Sagrantino is the near black red of Montefalco in Umbria: blackberry, incense and cocoa on a grip few wines can match.
lines.s20: Sagrantino is the grape of Montefalco in Umbria, made dry or as a sweet passito. It is near black, with blackberry, prune and incense, and a tannin so firm it wants years in bottle and a rich dish beside it.
lines.s45: Sagrantino grows almost nowhere but Montefalco, a hill town in Umbria, the green heart of Italy. Its thick skins give a near black wine of blackberry, black cherry and prune, with incense, cocoa and dried violet. It is full bodied, and its tannin grips harder than almost any grape you will meet. It must age more than three years before release, a year of that in wood, and it rewards ten years in bottle. Open it for wild boar, a grilled steak or aged pecorino. Until the dry wine arrived in the 1970s, it was made sweet, from grapes dried on racks for feast days.
lines.sale: Sagrantino grows almost nowhere but Montefalco, one hill town in Umbria, and it pours near black, with blackberry and incense. Opened early, it stands up to the wild boar or the steak.

glass.lead: Blackberry, black cherry and prune with incense, cocoa and dried violet, near opaque and full, on a tannin that grips like few others.

ladder.where: The higher ridge of Montefalco and the King Valley
The lower slopes towards Bevagna, Heathcote and McLaren Vale

glass.structure: Dry. Acidity medium plus, tannin high and mouth coating, alcohol medium plus to high, body full; deep purple, nearly opaque.

home.home: Montefalco in Umbria, with Bevagna, Gualdo Cattaneo, Castel Ritaldi and Giano dell'Umbria. Montefalco Sagrantino is the grape alone, dry or passito, the dry wine aged 37 months with 12 in wood. A share of it gives grip to Montefalco Rosso, a Sangiovese blend.
home.abroad: Australia grows a little, in McLaren Vale, Heathcote and the King Valley, and California a few rows; these tend to be riper and fleshier, the grip still firm.

service.temp: 61 to 64 degrees Fahrenheit, 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; the passito a little cooler.
service.glass: A large Bordeaux glass, which gives the dense wine room to breathe.
service.decant: Often helps a young secco: taste a sample, then decant. An old bottle only to leave its sediment.
service.age: Ten years and more, and even then it grips; Montefalco Rosso drinks far sooner.

with.dish: Wild boar ragù or braised boar
with.why: a rich, gamey meat for a fierce grip
protein and fat soften the tannin
salt and fat round off the grip
sweet blackberry and tannin meet bitter cocoa

labels.means: Sagrantino alone from Montefalco and four neighbouring communes; a DOCG since 1992, dry or passito.
Dry; printed to set the dry wine apart from the passito.
A sweet red from bunches dried on racks for weeks, the original wine of Montefalco.
A Sangiovese led red with a share of Sagrantino for grip; a different, lighter wine.
The older form of the same DOCG's name.

guest.q: Why does this wine make my whole mouth feel dry?
guest.a: That is tannin, and Sagrantino's thick skins hold more of it than almost any grape. Fat and protein in the food, a decanter and years in bottle all soften it.

guest.q: Is Montefalco Rosso the same wine?
guest.a: No. Montefalco Rosso is mostly Sangiovese with a share of Sagrantino, lighter and ready sooner. Montefalco Sagrantino is the grape alone, made to age.
It can be. For centuries it was made sweet from dried grapes, and the dry wine came only in the 1970s. Secco on the label means dry, passito means sweet.

compare.tell: Tannat matches the grip with cassis, blueberry and iron; Sagrantino brings black cherry preserve, incense and dried violet.
Aglianico carries higher acidity, with tar and smoke; Sagrantino is blacker and denser, with incense, cocoa and dried violet.
Sangiovese, which leads Montefalco Rosso, is paler, with sour cherry and dried oregano and a gentler grip; Sagrantino is near black and far more tannic.

cards.front: Montefalco Sagrantino: what must it hold, and how long does it age?
cards.back: Sagrantino alone. The dry wine ages at least 37 months, 12 of them in wood and 4 in bottle; the passito shares the DOCG.

cards.front: Sagrantino: how was it made before the 1970s, and what is passito?
cards.back: Sweet. Bunches were dried on racks for weeks and made into passito for feast days; dry Sagrantino is a wine of the 1970s.

cards.front: Montefalco Rosso and Montefalco Sagrantino: how do the two wines differ?
cards.back: Montefalco Rosso is a Sangiovese led blend with a share of Sagrantino, ready sooner. Montefalco Sagrantino is the grape alone, a DOCG made to age.

questions.q: A red poured blind is near opaque, with blackberry, prune, incense and cocoa, and a tannin that coats the whole mouth. The bottle is from Umbria. Which grape is it?
questions.exp: Near opaque colour, incense and cocoa on a tannin like few others point to Sagrantino of Montefalco. Sangiovese, Umbria's other red, is paler, with sour cherry and a gentler grip.

questions.q: A guest wants the sweet red of Montefalco to finish dinner. Which word on the label do you look for?
questions.exp: Passito marks the sweet wine made from bunches dried on racks for weeks. Secco, the nearest miss, marks the dry wine of the same DOCG.

questions.q: A guest enjoys the Montefalco Rosso by the glass and asks how the Montefalco Sagrantino on the list differs. What is the main difference?
opts: It is Sagrantino alone, not a Sangiovese blend
It is the sweet version of the Rosso
It comes from another region of Italy
It is aged without any wood
questions.exp: Montefalco Sagrantino is the grape alone, dense and tannic, aged 37 months. Montefalco Rosso, from the same hills, is led by Sangiovese with a share of Sagrantino.

report: Mode home, as the plan fixes it. Nothing contradicts TASTE.world old.

The rules (Sagrantino alone, 37 months with 12 in wood and 4 in bottle, dry or passito under one DOCG, DOC 1979 and DOCG 1992), the five communes, Montefalco Rosso as Sangiovese led with a share of Sagrantino, the dry wine as a wine of the 1970s after centuries of passito for the church calendar, and blackberry, dried plum and black tea all stand on the Codex's Umbria record; black cherry, cocoa, dried violet and incense on GRAPES_PLUS.

The passito history stands on Decanter as well (always sweet until the grape nearly vanished after the Second World War). The name is left out: sources tie it to the Latin sacer, the sacristy or a feast, and none settles it.

Abroad: McLaren Vale, Heathcote and the King Valley stand on Wine Companion, Decanter and Wine Selectors as search results quoted them; California, Washington and Texas on two trade pages. The hosts could not be opened in this session.
Lavender, clove and cinnamon rest on producers' and critics' tasting notes read through search, not on a reference work; a checker may prefer to cut lavender.

Alcohol: TASTE says medium plus (alc 2); the DOCG's floor and the wines a list carries run higher, so the structure line says medium plus to high. The tannin claim is said as more than almost any grape, not as the most tannic, though the Codex's Umbria record and GRAPES_PLUS go further.

checked.verdict: Sound after two fixes. Sagrantino alone, 37 months with 12 in wood and 4 in bottle, DOC 1979 and DOCG 1992, the five communes, dry or passito under one DOCG, the dry wine of the 1970s and Montefalco Rosso as a Sangiovese blend all stand on the Codex's Umbria record; lavender was one producer's note and a food reason named a family.
changed: glass.notes.2.notes: Lavender stood on one producer's tasting note found through search, as the author flagged; violet runs through every description read and the reviewed profile has dried violet. A blind taster nods at violet in a young wine and dried violet in an older one.
food.with.3.why: Black fruit is a family word standing alone in a reason that describes the glass; blackberry names it.
open: The Umbria record says Sagrantino has the highest tannin and polyphenol load measured in any Italian variety and GRAPES_PLUS calls it often the most tannic grape in the world: superlatives in reviewed records, not this entry's to change.
